title: 'To own a Razer Artisan Keycap is to display one’s allegiance, a mark of belonging within the Cult of Razer' says the PR nonsense behind this $90 coil of snakes
body: "To own a Razer Artisan Keycap is to display one’s allegiance, a mark of belonging within the cult of Razer," says the marketing gumph for the company's first artisan keycap . I've read a lot of ambitious press releases in this job, but that's definitely the strangest sentence I've parsed this year. That being said, I do like the look of the Razer Artisan Keycap - Triple-Headed Snake Edition . Because as the name suggests, it's made up of a twisting coil of snakes. Indiana Jones wouldn't approve, but as for Andy-ana Edser? Aye, it's alright by me. Razer's slippery new keycap is resin-cast, has been individually hand-painted (I'd genuinely enjoy that job), and subjected to a two-stage quality control process that makes sure no dust or bubbles are left on the final product. It's been designed to fit on MX-style, cross-stem switches, so it should be compatible with most keyboards. Even if you haven't bought into the cult of Razer and gone for a competitor's product instead. Which is probably some form of heresy in Razer's eyes, I would imagine. The keycap is also "the next step towards the ultimate expression of keyboard customisation," and "a statement of identity," apparently. My g…
